public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Normality of mathematical constants

Despite extensive empirical evidence—billions of digits have been computed for $\pi$,
$e$, and $\sqrt{2}$, all showing near-uniform digit distribution—it is an open problem
whether any of the classical constants $\pi$, $e$, $\sqrt{2}$, $\ln 2$, or $\varphi$ is
normal in any base.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia (Normal number)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number)
* [Wikipedia (Pi)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pi)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Real

namespace NormalNumber

/--
$\pi$ is normal in base 10.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem pi_normal_base_ten : IsNormalInBase 10 π := by
  sorry

end NormalNumber

reformulations.difference: The underlying IsNormalInBase definition allows block length zero and counts occurrences starting at every i < n, whereas the source describes positive-length blocks and counts occurrences wholly contained in the first n digits.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a fixed positive block length k, the two counts differ by at most k−1, so their normalized difference tends to zero. The empty-block condition is automatic: its frequency is n/n = 1 for every positive n, and the required limit is 10^0 = 1. Proved the full equivalence with positive-length, complete-substring counting in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and specialized it to base 10 and π; the proof has no sorry dependencies.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number — introduction, Definitions, Properties and examples, and Notes
Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean and Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean in the supplied checkout
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the decimal-normality conjecture for π. Checked digit extraction, real-valued frequencies, quantifier scope, zero-length blocks, and the n = 0 denominator. Lean tests confirm the expected digits of terminating decimals and that zero is not decimal-normal. Omitting π’s integer part does not affect limiting block frequencies. Both cited sources still describe π’s normality as unresolved, consistent with research open.
